items.body: `summarize_finish()` immediately calls `request_summary_finish()`, which signals the active agent through `reap_summary_children()`. It therefore kills an in-flight parse before the required 60-second wait.
items.suggestion: Mark finishing without killing the child, wait up to 60 seconds, and kill the process group only after timeout. Keep immediate cancellation as a separate mid-session-disable path.

items.body: The final parse runs after releasing the singleton guard. Concurrent `summarize-finish` calls can both select the same unseen records before either reservation updates the cursor, spawning two children and replaying paid input.
items.suggestion: Hold the parser singleton through final selection/reservation/invocation, and revalidate each record against `last_consumed_seq` under the state lock.
items.title: The final parse runs after releasing the singleton guard

items.body: `communicate()` buffers unlimited stdout/stderr, then stdout is sliced by characters. Over-limit output is accepted as a valid summary instead of killing the child and falling back. Result and notification limits are likewise character—not byte—limits.
items.suggestion: Stream bounded bytes, kill the process group on overflow, reject that invocation, bound stderr, and enforce byte-based stored-result and notification truncation.
items.title: `communicate()` buffers unlimited stdout/stderr, then stdout is sliced by characters

items.body: The debounce timestamp exists only in parser-process memory. After a parser crash, `last_started` resets to zero and unseen records invoke immediately, bypassing the 20-second replacement debounce.
items.suggestion: Persist the last invocation timestamp atomically with reservation and honor its remaining debounce after restart.
items.title: The debounce timestamp exists only in parser-process memory

items.body: Invocation failures are collapsed to an empty result with no durable failure state. Focus-off treats them identically to summaries-off, no-agent, or empty-input cases, so users are never told that parsing failed.
items.suggestion: Persist a session-scoped parse-failure status and report it after successful lift before invoking the grouped fallback.

items.body: `expected_session` is validated only after `request_summary_finish()` has already stopped the current session. A delayed stale `summarize-finish --session …` can terminate a newer session.
items.suggestion: Pass the expected session into the finish-state mutation and reject mismatches atomically before changing or signalling anything.

items.suggestion: Route a retained catch-up through the XOR cleanup after every successful lift, including the summaries-off grouped branch.
